1	# The report and the record
2	
3	## What every report holds
4	
5	Your brief says where your report goes: a file that it names, your final message, or both. If it names no file, your report is your final message.
6	
7	A finding is something that your work learned about the tree or the language, and that the record does not hold yet. Examples: a defect, a behaviour that departs from the specification or from a decision of the curator, a measurement. What you did along the way is not a finding, for example the files that you read or edited. Your transcript keeps that.
8	
9	A fact is a finding that is an established property of the tree, the language, the library or their tools, and that later work builds on. A defect also gets its ledger row, and a fact about it may cite the row.
10	
11	A point to report is a kind of change or finding that the curator wants to review. Your brief names its points to report. Examples: a changed line of a test that the team wrote, a checker edit inside a change to the library, a changed line of the model program.
12	
13	Put each of these that you have in your report, in this form, whatever else your brief asks for:
14	
15	- **Defects.** Each defect that you measured, and the test or ledger row that records it (`tests-writing.md`, "How a defect is recorded").
16	- **Sentences of the specification made false.** Each sentence of the specification that your change makes false, quoted with its file and line. Such a sentence says what walk or the compiled path does. It is in the effect of an Appendix I entry (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex`), or in a `\revision` or `\note{}` box beside a passage.
17	- **Decisions.** Each choice that you made among alternatives, as a decision apart from the findings: what you chose, the alternatives, and the evidence, cited. If no decision of the curator covers it, say so, and say which reading you acted on. A decision left as a line inside the findings counts as not made.
18	- **Points to report.** Each point that your brief names and the work reached, with its evidence, also one that only part of the work reached.
19	- **For FACTS.** Each fact that your work established, in the hand-over form of "Writing to the record". If your brief let you write FACTS, give instead the number of each entry that you added or rewrote. If your work established no fact, write "none".
20	- **Commands.** Each command that you had to work out because this skill does not give it, with what it does.
21	- **Questions for the curator.** If something needs the curator's decision, list it as a decision not taken, in the form that `exploring.md` gives. The reader of your report brings it to the curator. Do not choose which of your items anyone reviews.
22	
23	## At a point to report
24	
25	- If the work reaches a point to report, do what the brief says for it. For example, a brief can say that a defect in the code is recorded in a ledger row and not repaired.
26	- Then finish the work.
27	- If a step cannot be undone, or would change a decision of the curator, report it instead. List it as a decision not taken, with its alternatives.
28	
29	## Timings and citations
30	
31	- If you take a timing that you will keep, run nothing else beside it. All agents of the session share the machine's cores (the `cloud-container` skill).
32	- Name the machine with every timing: `nproc`, the CPU's model and MHz, the load at start, the JDK, `FORTRESS_THREADS`. Only a pair of timings taken in one run measures a difference.
33	- If you take a measurement again because the code changed, say what changed.
34	- In a report, cite the tree at file:line, and quote results, two to five lines, each with its command. Never cite a file under `tmp/`.
35	
36	## POSITIONS and FACTS
37	
38	POSITIONS and FACTS describe the present: no dates, no names of who found what, no "corrected" or "superseded" notes. The history of each entry is in `POSITIONS-history.md` and `FACTS-history.md`, beside them. When your work needs the detail of an entry, print the report section that it cites (`$T 'doc:PATH#HEADING'`, below). Read its history only when the tree disagrees with the entry.
39	
40	Each entry is one line that starts with its permanent number: `F-87` in FACTS, `P-48` in POSITIONS. A FACTS entry is the fact as it stands now, what it means for the work, and the test that fails if the fact stops holding, under a bold title. If no test checks the fact, the entry gives the command and the output that show it. It points to the report section that holds the detail. Cite an entry by its number. If the reader must know what the entry says without printing it, add the first words of its title in quotes: F-87, "The first words ...".
41	
42	## The gap ledger
43	
44	The ledger's rows are the bug reports that the work fixes. A fix of a row starts with its reproduction, written as a test (`tests-writing.md`).
45	
46	A row is one line of eight cells, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of a topic section. Reports cite a row by its number, which it keeps for good. A new issue gets a new row.
47	
48	- Its status is one of seven words: `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`, `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`, `CONTESTED`, `RETIRED`, `FIXED`, `DUPLICATE`. The last three close a row. The row template (below) defines each.
49	- Its class is a kind and an area, such as `implementation gap (checker)`.
50	- The earlier text of a changed row is in `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger-history.md`.
51	
52	Read the ledger only through the queries below: it is too large to read whole.
53	
54	Three limits of `ledger.py` (below):
55	
56	- A row at its 1,200-character limit takes no further note.
57	- No command edits a row's claim. `close --claim` takes a corrected one.
58	- Its heading reader does not expand the specification's `\Trait{X}` macro. So a row that names a library trait's section cites `Specification-1.0-frozen/` by line.
59	
60	## Reading the record
61	
62	Read only the slice of the record that you need. This tool prints whole entries, in parts of bounded size:
63	
64	    T=explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh
65	
66	- `$T 'F-87'` prints one entry by its number, and `$T 'P-48'` one of POSITIONS. `$T 'F-87+'` adds each entry that F-87 cites by its number, and each entry that cites F-87. `$T 'history:F-87'` prints its history. Run one when your brief or a note cites an entry by its number.
67	- `$T 'positions:WORDS OF A TITLE'` prints one of the curator's decisions. Run it before you choose among ways to do something. If several titles hold the words, it names them.
68	- `$T 'WORDS OF A TITLE'` prints each FACTS entry whose bold title holds them, and `$T 'section:HEADING'` every entry of a FACTS section. Run one before you investigate a behaviour of the tree, and when your brief or a note names an entry. These queries and `positions:` read titles only: before you write that the record does not hold something, also grep FACTS and POSITIONS for its words.
69	- `$T 'index:WORDS'` prints the INDEX lines that hold the words. Run it to find the notes on a topic.
70	- `$T 'ledger-find:WORDS'` prints one line for each ledger row that holds every word. Run it when you meet a defect, before you investigate it.
71	- `$T 'ledger:ROW'` prints one row whole. Run it for each row that you need from a find, your brief or a note.
72	- `$T 'doc:PATH#HEADING'` prints a section of any note, or of a `.tex` chapter, and `$T 'map:FILE#HEADING'` a section of a note under `explorations/coordinator/map/`. Run one when your brief or a note names a section. `#HEADING@WORDS` prints only the table rows and list items of that section that hold every one of WORDS.
73	- `$T --check QUERY ...` prints only where each query matches and its size. Run it before a query whose size you do not know. `--part N` prints part N of a long output, and `--help` gives the rest.
74	
75	A word of a query that ends in `*` matches the start of a word. Any other word matches a whole word.
76	
77	Before you edit a file of the original tree, list the ledger rows that cite it, and read each row that your edit can change:
78	
79	    python3 explorations/coordinator/tools/ledger.py find --cites FILE
80	
81	## Writing to the record
82	
83	- Write FACTS and POSITIONS only with `explorations/coordinator/tools/record.py`, never by hand. `add` gives a new entry its number, and `set` rewrites an entry. The tool writes the entry to `FACTS.md` or `POSITIONS.md`, and its earlier text to the history file beside it. It commits nothing: commit both files in one commit. Its header gives its usage.
84	- If your brief lets you write FACTS, add each fact as a new entry in the section of its topic, in the commit that establishes it. Put its detail in a section of your report: the file:line citations, the commands with their output, and the measured numbers. Point the entry to that section, by your report's file and the section's heading. If your report is only your final message, hand the fact over instead. Spend no effort on the entry's wording: it is rewritten to the record's form after your work.
85	- If your brief does not let you write FACTS, hand each fact over in the "For FACTS" item of your report, with:
86	  - the fact as it stands now, in one sentence;
87	  - what it means for the work;
88	  - the number that a decision rests on, if any, with what it counts; if its parts belong to different ledger rows, the part of each row;
89	  - the test that fails if the fact stops holding, or the command and the output that show it;
90	  - the section of your report that holds the detail.
91	- If your brief lets you write FACTS, rewrite a wrong entry in place. Otherwise say in your hand-over that the entry is wrong, with the evidence.
92	- POSITIONS holds each of the curator's decisions, in one place. Everything else points there. Write a decision there only if your brief gives it to you to record. If you have evidence against one, do as `exploring.md` says.
93	- Put new files of the work under `explorations/`. If you add a note directly in `explorations/` or `explorations/reviews/`, add its line to INDEX: ``- `PATH`: `` and the first sentence of the note's header comment.
94	
95	Write the gap ledger only with `ledger.py`, which checks each line that it writes against the row template.
96	
97	    L="python3 explorations/coordinator/tools/ledger.py"
98	
99	To add a row:
100	
101	1. Print the row template, about 3 KB: `$T 'doc:explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md#The row template'`.
102	2. Write the row as one line in a file under your tree's `tmp/`, with `?` in its number cell.
103	3. Run `$L add FILE --section TITLE`. It numbers the row and puts it in that section. If the row breaks the template, it adds nothing and prints each rule broken. `$L sections` lists the titles.
104	
105	To change a row:
106	
107	- `$L note N TEXT` adds TEXT to the notes of row N.
108	- `$L duplicate N --of M` makes row N a pointer to row M.
109	- `$L close N --commit HASH --test NAME` marks row N `FIXED`, by the commit HASH and its test NAME. Run it once that commit is in `HEAD`, and commit the close after it.
110	
111	## The repository's history
112	
113	- The repository is a 2018 fork of `sirinath/fortress`, a git conversion of the project's java.net Mercurial repository. Its trunk runs from 2007-01-04 to 2012-08-31 and ends at `a874948ac`, the team's last commit.
114	- The commits after `a874948ac` are the revival's. After the tag `sealed-tree`, commit `75cca6683`, the revival began to fix the team's code, test first. Before it, the revival changed mainly the build and the toolchain.
115	- `git diff a874948ac -- FILE` shows what the revival changed in a file, and `git diff 75cca6683 -- FILE` what it changed after the tag.
116	- The conversion cut 146 parent links, so a `git log` of a directory stops at a cut and misses the team's earlier commits. Use `git log --follow` on a file, or compare contents.
117	- To find who wrote something, or where the repository's history after 2012 comes from, read `research/authorship.md` and `explorations/coordinator/lineage.md`.
118	- Commit `8fe1daa8f` copied a third-party port of the tree to Java 9 onto the team's last commit, `a874948ac`. Give its lines no credit, and name no author of it in any text that you commit. In a reconstruction of authorship, attribute nothing of it to anyone.

1	# Committing and pushing
2	
3	**scratch**
4	: Files and folders that your work makes and `main` does not keep: logs, captured and raw run output, copies of tools, probe programs, lists and private caches folders.
5	
6	Your brief says whether you commit and push, and on which branch. If it says nothing, commit on your current branch, and push it.
7	
8	## What to commit
9	
10	- Commit your change, its tests, your report if it is a file, and any reusable script.
11	- Commit what you write to the record, such as a ledger row, with the work that it records. A row's close follows the fix's commit (`records.md`).
12	- Keep scratch in your tree's `tmp/`, which is gitignored.
13	- In a fresh clone, `.claude/worktrees/` and `.claude/agents/` show as untracked, because the lines of `.git/info/exclude` that hide them are not in the clone. Do not commit them.
14	- Keep a copyrighted PDF or deck in `research/decks/`, which is gitignored. Cite it by its Wayback URL. Notes on it go in `research/extracts/`: your own summary, with brief attributed quotations.
15	- Put provenance and rationale in commit messages and reports, not in source comments.
16	- Name a model by its tier (Opus, Sonnet, Fable) in any text that you commit, commit messages included. Never write its model identifier, the API's name for the model, which starts with `claude-`.
17	
18	## How to commit
19	
20	Commit as you go, each commit in one command that names its paths:
21	
22	    git add -- <paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <paths>
23	
24	- The command commits only the paths that it names. Other agents may have uncommitted edits in your tree. Leave them alone.
25	- If you renamed a file with `git mv`, name its old path in `git commit` only, because `git add` refuses a path that no longer exists: `git add -- <new paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <new paths> <old paths>`.
26	- Never commit a copied directory, and never use `git add -A`.
27	- Before you commit more than a few hundred lines, stage them and read what you staged: `git add -- <paths> && git diff --cached --stat -- <paths>`.
28	- If the commit edits the original tree, say so in its message.
29	- End every commit message with this footer, exactly, whatever footer Claude Code suggests:
30	
31	      Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
32	      Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AmiXNpJxQ6TBwec4vJZHDB
33	
34	  If your brief gives another session line, use it.
35	
36	## Pushing
37	
38	Push after every commit, so that a lost container loses nothing.
39	
40	- If you work on your own branch, push it: `git push -u origin <branch>` the first time, then `git push`. Your brief says how the branch reaches `main`.
41	- If you work on `main`, other agents commit to it too. Push only your own commits:
42	  1. Run `git log origin/main..main`. Your commits are those whose hashes your own `git commit` printed.
43	  2. If it lists another agent's commit, run the command again shortly: that agent pushes right after it commits. If the commit stays, push nothing, and say so in your report.
44	  3. If it lists only your commits, push three times, in this order:
45	
46	         git push origin main
47	         git push origin main:claude/worker-brief-fable-vnnuv8
48	         git push origin main:blinded-fable
49	
50	     The third push keeps `blinded-fable` current. If the container is lost, the platform rebuilds it from that branch.
51	- Push no branch that this section does not name, unless your brief names it.
52	- If a push is refused, push nothing more, and say so in your report.

1	# Writing a test
2	
3	**gated test**
4	: Test that the gate's suites run.
5	
6	**green**
7	: Harness's report on a test that JUnit counts as passed.
8	
9	**red**
10	: Harness's report on a test that JUnit counts as failed.
11	
12	**`XXX` test**
13	: Gated expected failure. It asserts the answer that the specification gives, and fails today. The harness reports it green while it fails, and red when the defect is fixed.
14	
15	## A test program
16	
17	A test program has this form:
18	
19	    component Name
20	    export Executable
21	
22	    (* declarations *)
23	
24	    run(): () = do
25	        assert(f(2), 4, "f(2)")
26	    end
27	
28	    end
29	
30	- `(*)` starts a comment to the end of the line. It cannot hold `*)`: the parser ends the comment there and refuses the program. `(* ... *)` comments nest.
31	- A compiled test with a `run` key ends `run()` with `println("PASS")`, unless a `run_out` key checks its output (below).
32	- Under walk, `assert(x, y, msg)` checks that `x` equals `y`, for values of any type. The compiler's library declares the two-value `assert` only for `ZZ32`, `String` and `Character`; its `assert(flag, msg)` takes any `Boolean`.
33	- Do not name a variable or a parameter after a functional method of the library, such as `big`, `even`, `numerator` or `shift`. The disambiguator, the phase that binds names, refuses it: "Variable even is already declared."
34	- Under walk, a numeral does not bind to `NN32` or `NN64`, and a numeral with a radix point does not bind to `RR32` (ledger row 454). Write `a: NN32 = unsigned(5)`, not `a: NN32 = 5`.
35	
36	## Where a test goes, and how it passes
37	
38	Interpreter (walk): write `ProjectFortress/tests/Name.fss`, whose component is `Name`.
39	
40	- Every `.fss` file there is gated, with no `.test` file needed.
41	- It is green if it throws no exception, exits 0, and neither its standard output nor its standard error contains `fail` or `FAIL`. A longer word counts too: `failure` fails the test. Only a file whose name contains `QuickCheckTest` is exempt.
42	- An api that it imports, and a helper component, go in `ProjectFortress/test_library/`. In `tests/`, a helper would run as a test.
43	- The harness skips files whose names end in `Syntax.fss`, `DynamicSemantics.fss` or `Satisfiability.fss`, or contain `GenomeUtil`.
44	- For a refusal at load, put `Name.test` beside `tests/Name.fss`, with `load_exception_contains=<message>`. A plain test is green if walk refuses the program at load as named. A failure while the top-level variables are initialised counts as a refusal. An `XXX` test with such a `.test` file is green if the program loads and runs clean.
45	
46	Compiled: write `Name.fss` and `Name.test` in the compiled test folder that holds tests of its kind:
47	
48	- `library_tests/`: the compiler's library. A test of the interpreter's library is an interpreter test (above).
49	- `parser_tests/`: the parser.
50	- `compiler_tests/`: the rest, beside the team's numbered `CompiledN` tests.
51	- `other_compiler_tests/`: the team's compiled tests that do not fit the `CompiledN` series, by the comment in `OtherCompilerJUTest.java`. Put no new test there.
52	
53	The `.test` files are the whole list of tests: a `.fss` that no `.test` file names never runs. A `.test` file is a Java property file. It names the commands to run and the checks on their output, as lit's RUN and CHECK lines do:
54	
55	    tests=Name                 the component(s) it drives; without it, the .test file's own name
56	    compile | link | typecheck each present command is one JUnit case; link compiles, then links
57	    run                        run the linked program in a subprocess (bin/fortress run)
58	    <command>_<stream>_<check>=text
59	                               command: compile, link or run; stream: out, err or exception;
60	                               check: contains, does_not_contain, equals, matches,
61	                               WIcontains (containment with runs of whitespace collapsed)
62	
63	A `run` fails if the program exits non-zero or a `run_*` check fails. With no `run_out` check, its output must contain `pass` or `PASS`. For example:
64	
65	    tests=EqualityRung1
66	    link
67	    run
68	    run_out_WIcontains=PASS
69	
70	## How `XXX` works
71	
72	- Under walk, an `XXX` test is `tests/XXXName.fss`, whose component is `XXXName`. With no `.test` file, it is green when it fails as a plain test would.
73	- In the compiled test folders, the `XXX` prefix of a `.test` file's name applies to every command that the file drives: each must fail. So a defect at run time, whose link succeeds, needs two `.test` files ("Writing an `XXX` test").
74	- An unmet `run_*` check makes a run test red, whatever the prefix.
75	- The harness reports any link or compile exception of a component whose name contains `XXX` as expected, whatever the `.test` file's name. Only an unmet key of that command makes it red.
76	- An `XXX` compile test with a `compile_err_contains` key, whose program compiles, reports "Saw wrong failure", which is red.
77	- A green `XXX` test prints `Saw expected failure` or `OK Saw expected exception`.
78	
79	## How a defect is recorded
80	
81	Record every defect that you measure in one of three ways, and say in your report which:
82	
83	1. Your change repairs it: an assertion in your plain gated test. It needs no `XXX` stage.
84	2. It is deferred, and the specification settles it: a gated `XXX` test that asserts the specification's answer. Write it in the change that measured the defect, even if a later change will repair it. A deferred defect of a program that the checker accepts and that then fails the JVM's verification (`VerifyError`), linkage or a range check at run time is one of these.
85	3. It is deferred, and the specification is silent or a conflict leaves it open (`exploring.md`): a test that asserts today's behaviour, and a row in the gap ledger (`records.md`). If no program can observe the defect, or no gated test can pass while it shows, as when walk crashes on the program, write the ledger row only. Its reproducer, the row's cell that names the test, is `none`, and its notes give the command and its output.
86	
87	If your brief does not let you edit the original tree, say in your report which of the three the defect needs, and write a ledger row for it, whichever it needs. A probe that only measures and reports is an example. The change that next works there writes the test.
88	
89	## The order: the test, its failure, the fix, the pass
90	
91	1. Write the test, with a plain name. Write the essence of the defect as a clean, minimal program, not the shape in which a probe met it.
92	2. See the test fail through the harness (`harness-one.sh` or `junit.sh`, `tests-running.md`) on the base's code. Do this in a run that ends before you first build or compile your edit. Under walk, do it before you edit a library source that the test reads. If your tree already holds the fix, run the test through the harness on the old code, as `worktrees.md`, "Running the old code", says.
93	3. Make the fix. See the test pass in your last run after your last change of code.
94	
95	The test needs no commit of its own. A test that comes with no fix, such as one that guards a behaviour that works today, has no failing run: see it pass through the harness.
96	
97	In your report, quote two to five lines of the failing run, if there is one, and the passing line, each with its command. In an edit of the original tree, put every check into a gated test, never into a one-off script. A probe that only measures may use its own script. Assert a value with `assert` in an interpreter test. In a compiled test, assert it with `assert` (above), or print it and check it with a `run_out_equals` key. The harness checks both, so they are part of the suite's verdict.
98	
99	An edit of prose in `Specification/` or `Documentation/` has no test. Check it as `specification.md`, "Changing the text: the revision form", says.
100	
101	## Writing an `XXX` test
102	
103	In a compiled test folder, name the component `XXXName`, in its file `XXXName.fss` and in its `component` line.
104	
105	- For a refusal at compile time, write one `XXX` compile test, with `compile` and `compile_err_contains=<the refusal's message>`.
106	- For a code-generator wall (`compiler.md`, "What the compiled path cannot compile yet"), write `XXXName.test` with `tests=XXXName`, `compile` and `compile_exception_contains=<text of the exception>`.
107	- For a program that compiles and fails at run time, write two `.test` files over the component:
108	  - `NameLink.test`, a plain name, with `tests=XXXName` and `link`. It is red if the link reports static errors, but green on an exception.
109	  - `XXXName.test`, with `tests=XXXName` and `run`, and no `link`. Its run uses the plain file's link, so run the two files in one call of `junit.sh` or `fortress junit`, the plain one first.
110	  - The program prints `REACHED` in `run()` before the part that fails. The `XXX` file checks it with `run_out_contains=REACHED`, or with `run_out_does_not_contain=REACHED` if the run dies before `run()` prints. Never use `run_out_contains=PASS`.
111	  - Example: `compiler_tests/XXXBoxDotSpellingsRungW.test` and `BoxDotSpellingsRungWLink.test`.
112	
113	Show the first `XXX` test that your change adds, and only the first, working through the harness (`harness-one.sh`, `junit.sh` or `fortress junit`), from its place in a gated test folder. A direct compile and run does not show this. Run it twice:
114	
115	1. As it is: the harness must report an expected failure.

1	# The library
2	
3	The library is `Library/` and `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/`, without the compiler's own files there:
4	
5	- In `Library/`: the interpreter's prelude, `FortressLibrary.fss` and `.fsi`, and its other components. The compiler's `CompilerLibrary`, `CompilerAlgebra` and `CompilerSystem` are not part of it. `FortressAst.fss` and `.fsi` are generated from `ProjectFortress/astgen/Fortress.ast`: edit that file, never these two.
6	- In `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/`: `FortressBuiltin`, `NativeArray` and the rest. The compiler's `CompilerBuiltin` is not part of it.
7	- `LibraryBuiltin/AnyType`, the top type, belongs to both libraries. After an edit to it, also take the compiled path's step (`build-and-caches.md`, "After an edit of the library").
8	- `Library/incomplete/` is not on the source path (`default_repository/configuration`), so no program can import what it declares. Nothing that the suites or the model program run imports `Library/GeneratorLibrary.fss` either. Before you cite a declaration as the library's way, check that a running program can reach it.
9	
10	## How loops and reductions call the library
11	
12	The desugarer, which both paths share, turns these forms into calls of the library:
13	
14	- `for x <- g do b end` becomes `g.loop(fn x => b)`, a call of the generator's `loop` method. Each further generator nests one more `loop` call inside.
15	- `while x <- e do b end` becomes `while __whileCond(e, fn x => b) do end`. `if x <- e then ... end` becomes a call of `__cond`.
16	- A comprehension or a big operator, such as `SUM`, becomes a call of `__bigOperator`, whose argument calls `__generate` on each generator. A big operator inside another becomes one call of `__bigOperator2`.
17	
18	These functions work on the library's generators and reductions: `trait Generator` and `trait Reduction` in `FortressLibrary.fsi`, and `RangeInternals.fss` for ranges. `FortressLibrary.fss` also defines `__loop`, but no desugaring calls it. So a failure inside a loop or a reduction is most often in the library's code, and its fix is a library edit.
19	
20	## The curator's decisions on the library
21	
22	- Scalar ranges are over `ZZ32` only. A range over another integer type is a static error, and walk stops when it builds one. Write a wider counter as a `ZZ32` loop that widens its index.
23	- `ZZ32` and numerals convert into `RR64` implicitly. `ZZ64` converts into `RR64` only explicitly, by `asFloat`.
24	- For arithmetic that wraps on overflow, use the wrapping operators ∔ `DOTPLUS`, ∸ `DOTMINUS` and ⨰ `DOTTIMES`. Parenthesise every such expression fully, because their precedence is stated only among themselves.
25	- `SUM` and `PROD` are generic over `AdditiveGroup` and `MultiplicativeRing`. If nothing at the call fixes the element type, write it: `SUM[\ZZ32\][j <- 0#n] f(j)`. The checker refuses a call without it (ledger row 425). Walk runs such a call, but an empty one gives `ZZ32`'s identity (ledger row 645), and `Set`'s `BIG UNION` and `BIG INTERSECTION` stop (ledger row 662).
26	- An array's `fill` takes a value, and its `tabulate` a function of the index: `array[\ZZ32\](4).fill(0)`, `array[\ZZ32\](4).tabulate(fn (i:ZZ32):ZZ32 => 10 i)`. The factories that take a function are `tabulatedArray1` to `tabulatedArray3` and `tabulatedVector`.
27	
28	## Designing a change
29	
30	- Put each extension into this library, outside the compiler's files. This includes an extension that only the model program needs.
31	- Fix a gap in the library, not by a workaround in the program that meets it. Take the design from the library's practice as well as from the specification's text. If the two disagree, do as `specification.md`, "When the text and an implementation disagree", says.
32	- If a rule of the language or the checker refuses the way that you want, find how the library writes that kind of thing. Do the same. The checker's refusals of this library reach you only through your brief: `fortress typecheck` checks against the compiler's prelude.
33	- When you add a method, make it dotted or functional as its family in the library does. If the family shows no practice, follow the team's proposal, which no program can import (`Library/incomplete/Collection.fss`): an updater, a getter or a setter, indexing included, is dotted, and every other method is functional.
34	- A new functional method reserves its name in every program that imports the library. The phase that binds names then refuses each program that names a variable or a parameter after it: "Variable even is already declared."
35	- A dotted method shadows a top-level function of the same name (`overloading.tex`, "Principles of Overloading").
36	- A new overload can make walk refuse every program at load. `interpreter.md`, "What walk checks", lists what walk refuses.
37	- A new native is a Java class under `interpreter/glue/prim/` (`interpreter.md`, "Natives"), so it is an edit of walk's Java too.
38	- `interpreter.md`, "The model program", says how to check microGPT under walk.
39	
40	## Editing
41	
42	A comment after a declaration that ends in an expression or a type becomes part of that declaration's source span. It also becomes part of the unambiguous name made from the span. So a comment-only edit changes the syntax tree. Before you compare parse trees or diagnostics across such an edit, map their positions back to the lines before the edit. Three removed scripts did this: `parse-compare.sh`, `ast-compare.py` and `remap-lines.py`. Print one with `git show ab067d9b6^:explorations/compile-ladder/rung-library-comments/<name>`.
43

## 1. What changed, and why

- **The crash (row 684).** `TypeSchemaAnalyzer.boundsSubstitution` (David Chase, 2012, "TODO: FIX THIS FOR OPS") built each image variable's bound list from `conjuncts(imageTa.meet(e))` and cast every conjunct to `BaseType` (`TypeSchemaAnalyzer.scala:474-477` at a1a75716a). Take a bound list in which one bound is a trait with a `comprises` clause and another bound excludes one of its listed types. The analyzer's meet of that list is a union of intersections. So the cast threw whenever the overloading checker compared two overloads that carry such a list (`reduceED` `:421`, `normalizeED` `:216`, `subtypeEDInner` `:171`).
  - The bounds are now kept as the list they are, each already a `BaseType`, without `Any` and duplicates (`:471-480`).
  - The final check asks, bound by bound, that each variable's image is below each of its bounds' images. It asks no proof for a bound that the image variable was itself given (`:482-495`).
  - The revival's earlier change in this method, which keeps the size parameters as they are (3f297441c), stays.
- **Row 660.** The `SMathPrimary` case gives its expected type to a tight juxtaposition of items none of which is a function (`impls/Operators.scala:362-386`).
  - The multifix application is tried without the expected type. Where it applies, it is checked again with the expected type, and that check is kept if it succeeds.
  - Otherwise the binary applications are left-associated. The inner ones are checked as before, and the outermost with the expected type.
  - This is the loose juxtaposition's form since climb batch 11's rung E, and the repeated operator's since batch 12's rung C.
- **Fork 2's library half, built and held (Q13.2).** It was built as the judgement's default (d3d31b5b2): `T extends { Number, MultiplicativeRing[\T\] }` on 29 lines of `Library/FortressLibrary.fss` and 32 of `.fsi`, a bound per operator on the scalar block (8 and 8 lines), and `v.zero` off the diagonal in `matrix(v)`. It was measured, then taken back (816251130).
  - With the crash gone, the api's overloading check runs. Over the two-trait bound it takes about 17 minutes of a full core, where the base takes seconds, and the checker-count stage stops at 900 s (section 7).
  - The cause is in `TypeAnalyzer.scala`, rung N's file this batch. Every subtype query on a variable with that bound list expands `Number`'s `comprises` clause (row 688).
  - So the 23 sites and row 437 stay. The curator's question is in section 10.
- **The specification.** Appendix I's entry "The contexts that give a call an expected type" now says that the checker gives the tight juxtaposition its expected type, with the date and row 660 (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:2077-2088`).

- **Row 684**, the crash in `boundsSubstitution`: home 1, repaired; `OverloadTwoBoundsClosedTrait`.
- **Row 660**, the tight juxtaposition: home 1, repaired; `InferTightJuxtContext`.
- **Row 686**, a refused call, 'not applicable to an argument of type Box[\T\]'. The call's argument carries the caller's own two-bound type parameter: the form of the norm's call at `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2483` on the judgement's library copy.

  - Its cause is not `boundsSubstitution`: the refusal stands after the fix, at `Functionals.scala:721`.
- **Row 687**, a crash in `Formula.slv` (`Formula.scala:593`), 'Applied a substitution to an And and got an Or', on a call that converts a numeral beside such a parameter. Home 2, `XXXCoerceTwoBoundsClosedTrait`, for the same reason. `Formula.scala` is rung N's file.
- **Row 689** (the skeptic's), a crash in `Formula.slv` on a call whose argument is the caller's own two-bound type parameter, the brief's form of the second test: home 2, `XXXCallerParamTwoBoundsClosedTrait`.
- **Row 690** (the skeptic's), a valid overloading refused: a generic declaration with the bound list beside a declaration on the closed trait with the same return type gets a false Return Type Rule error where the base crashed: home 2, `XXXReturnRuleTwoBoundsClosedTrait`.
- **Row 691** (the skeptic's, the base's defect), a generic function's call with more arguments than parameters accepted and the extra ones dropped, a tight juxtaposition of four items among them: home 3, a row only, since a refusal the program should get cannot be an expected failure while the program compiles.
- **Row 688**, the analyzer's cost on a variable bounded by `{ Number, MultiplicativeRing[\T\] }`, with the overloading memo off as the count stage runs it: home 3, a row only, since no gated test can wait 17 minutes. Its notes give the command and the times. `TypeAnalyzer.scala` is rung N's file.
- **Row 685**, the two factory sites (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2454`, `:2831`): home 3, a row, as the brief gives it. Its reproducer is the distance stage's per-site list. `TypeWellFormedChecker.scala` is rung N's file. Not traced further.

#!/bin/bash
# count-run.sh <work-dir> [list-file] [shadow-classes-dir] [shards]: runs every file of [list-file] under
# `walk`, one JVM per test, and writes its output to <work-dir>/log/<test>.txt with an rc= secs= trailer.
# Without a list file (or with -), the list is every ProjectFortress/tests/*.fss of the tree the script sits
# in, generated at run time.  The list run goes to <work-dir>/list.txt and the pass's tree, commit and times
# to <work-dir>/pass.txt, which compare-normalised.py beside this script reads.
# The named one-time count of a batch record (climb-batch-workflow.md, "Preparing a batch record"): one base
# pass, started by the coordinator on the batch's base before the launch, and one edit pass, started by the
# rung worker after its last edit, compared by compare-normalised.py with the tests that vary from run to
# run listed in unstable.txt beside it (postmortem-2026-09-29/synthesis.md, section 2(a);
# postmortem-2026-09-29/measures-6.5b.md, "The interpreter tests that vary from run to run").
# Batch N's rung M's copy (git show 9269f7bd2^:explorations/compile-ladder/rung-integer-minmax/count-run.sh),
# rung F's runner, moved here four directories below the tree, its list generated when none is given.
# The shape of explorations/reviews/mie-probes/keep/nestprobe/run-tests.sh without its NestProbe shadow:
# each shard has its own FORTRESS_CACHES, so default_repository/ is never read or written and no two JVMs
# share a cache.  A shadow classes directory, if given, is put ahead of ProjectFortress/build on the classpath.
# A relative <work-dir> or list file is taken from the tree's root; a pass resumed in the same <work-dir>
# skips every test whose log has its trailer and appends to pass.txt.  Stop a pass only by its own path,
# never by this script's name across the box (climb-batch-workflow.md, "Shared prefix").
set -u
cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../../.."                            # $FORTRESS_HOME
# env.sh without its rm of /tmp/fortress*rats, which a parallel agent's runs may be using
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64 PATH="/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64/bin:$PATH" FORTRESS_HOME="$(pwd)" FORTRESS_THREADS=1
unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
U='usage: count-run.sh <work-dir> [list-file|-] [shadow-classes-dir] [shards]'
W=$(mkdir -p "${1:?$U}" && cd "$1" && pwd)
L=${2:--}
SH=${3:-}
N=${4:-4}
mkdir -p "$W/log"
if [ "$L" = - ]; then
  LC_ALL=C ls ProjectFortress/tests/*.fss > "$W/list.txt"
else
  [ "$L" -ef "$W/list.txt" ] || cp "$L" "$W/list.txt"
fi
CP=$(./bin/fortress_classpath 2>/dev/null | tail -1)
[ -n "$SH" ] && CP="$SH:$CP"
# one core per JVM, as the precedent: four run at once
FAST="-XX:+UseSerialGC -XX:TieredStopAtLevel=1 -XX:ActiveProcessorCount=1"
{
  echo "root=$FORTRESS_HOME"
  echo "work=$W"
  echo "commit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
  echo "changed=$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no | wc -l) tracked files differ from the commit"
  echo "tests=$(grep -c . "$W/list.txt")"
  echo "shadow=${SH:-none} shards=$N"
  echo "start=$(date -u +%FT%TZ) load: $(cut -d' ' -f1-3 /proc/loadavg)"
} | tee -a "$W/pass.txt"
for i in $(seq 0 $((N-1))); do
  (
    C="$W/caches-$i"; T="$W/tmp-$i"; mkdir -p "$C" "$T"
    [ -f "$C/global.map" ] || printf '\0\0\0\0' > "$C/global.map"
    awk -v n=$N -v i=$i 'NR % n == i' "$W/list.txt" | while read -r f; do
      t=$(basename "$f" .fss)
      grep -q '^rc=' "$W/log/$t.txt" 2>/dev/null && continue
      start=$(date +%s)
      FORTRESS_CACHES="$C" timeout -k 10 600 \
        java -Xmx4g -Xss64m -Djava.io.tmpdir="$T" $FAST -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -cp "$CP" com.sun.fortress.Shell walk "$f" \
        < /dev/null > "$W/log/$t.txt" 2>&1
      rc=$?
      printf '\nrc=%s secs=%s\n' "$rc" "$(( $(date +%s) - start ))" >> "$W/log/$t.txt"
    done
  ) &
done
wait
rm -f ProjectFortress/tests/poem.out
echo "done=$(date -u +%FT%TZ) logs: $(grep -l '^rc=' "$W"/log/*.txt | wc -l)" | tee -a "$W/pass.txt"

#!/bin/bash
# The gate's distance stage: the compiled checker over the whole interpreter library, the
# twelve prelude apis and their twelve components, every stage of every unit run whatever
# the earlier stages reported, so that nothing hides behind an early return; one table.
#
# Why it exists: Pavol's answer 11 (POSITIONS.md, 2026-09-26): the full measurement of the
# distance to the switch-over "becomes a report-only stage of phase 3's gates, whose job is
# driving it down". The checker-count stage beside it (../checker-count/run.sh) sees only
# the errors before each api's early return, 62 of about 1,740 on 2026-09-27.
#
# Run from $FORTRESS_HOME with explorations/experiment/env.sh sourced, after ant compileAll:
#
#     explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh <out-file> [scratch-dir] [setting]
#
# It writes the table to <out-file> and prints it. Nothing in the tree is touched: the
# shadow sources and classes, the driver, the checker's caches (-Dfortress.caches) and the
# JVM's temporary directory (so Rats! leaves nothing in /tmp) go to the scratch directory
# (default: $TMPDIR or /tmp), and the caches are deleted at the end. It never removes
# /tmp/fortress*rats, which other runs on the machine use. Exit 0 if the table was
# produced, 1 if it could not be. One JVM, -Xmx4g, one busy core: 789 s on the idle 4-CPU
# container on 2026-09-27, 14 to 24 minutes under load 7 to 18 (switch-over-distance-flat.md
# section 5); the table's #seconds and #machine rows say what each run took and where.
#
# The setting: "any" by default, the compiled path with the implicit bound Any
# (DistanceMulti's -setting any: the extends-Object pre-desugaring off, as walk's, and the
# compiled-expression desugaring on, as the compile path's). Answer 11 names the compile
# path's setting; batch 7's question 1, answered (a) on 2026-09-27 (POSITIONS.md, the
# numerics plans), bounds an unbounded type parameter by Any, and under it the switch-over
# takes that bound for the compiled path (CLIMB-BATCH-7.md section 1, Q1), so the 372
# "bound Object" errors of the plain compile setting are the setting's, not the library's
# (switch-over-distance-flat.md sections 2.7 and 5: "under (a) the stage runs stage-any").
# On the tree of 2026-09-27 it differs from walk's setting by the compiled-expression
# desugaring's 12 abstract-method errors on bodyless functions, one export error and the
# variance checker's crash on Stream: 1,746 to 1,747 against 1,737 to 1,738 (FACTS.md,
# "The true distance to the switch-over"). The third argument, walk or compile, runs
# another setting, for a comparison with the measurements on file; the gate never passes it.
#
# The overloading checker's memo is off (-Dfortress.analyzer.overload.cache=false), as in
# every run of the measurement: keyed on declaration pairs, it hides 27 to 35 errors
# depending on the build order (FACTS.md, "The overloading checker's memo hides errors
# by build order, so every count runs with it off ...").
#
# The sources beside this script are copies, taken 2026-09-27, so that the gate does not
# depend on a probe directory, as the checker-count stage's were: DistanceMulti.java from
# perf-probes/prelude/switch-over-distance-flat/ (35ef70584); shadow-patch.py from
# perf-probes/prelude/desugar-codegen/ (e5d8cdbd2); add-patch.py and errors.py from
# perf-probes/prelude/switch-over-distance/ (a7e3df9ad, 14d2f9839); classify.py from
# perf-probes/prelude/distance-triage/ (e17a9badc); all unchanged but classify.py, which since
# row 577 finds the library places that name three of its classes by their declarations in
# the tree's sources ($FH, passed to table.py), not by line ranges. table.py is new: it
# counts as those scripts count and prints the rows below. The shadow classes are not
# copies: they are made from the tracked sources at every run by text edits that must each
# match exactly once (shadow-patch.py, add-patch.py), so there is no copied checker to go
# stale silently; an edit that no longer matches stops the run before the checker starts,
# and the table then says so in its #shadow row, with no counts.
#
# The table, tab-separated, every row tagged:
#   #distance   the setting, the switches and the twelve targets
#   #total      distinct errors
#   #kind       by kind (errors.py): exclusion, comprises, overloading, return-type, ...
#   #class      by root cause (classify.py, distance-triage.md section 2), with its name
#   #check      a disagreement: errors.py's and table.py's totals, or sites classify.py cannot
#               find in the tree's library source
#   #unit       by the unit that printed the error first
#   #crash      each declaration, stage or target the checker crashed on
#   #seconds    the run's wall time, and FortressLibrary's, the part that takes it
#   #machine    nproc, CPU model and MHz, load at start, JDK, FORTRESS_THREADS
#   #shadow     whether every shadow edit matched the tracked sources; the last row
# ../distance/compare.sh compares two tables. The run-to-run variation is 2 to 4 errors,
# in the comparisons' and Maybe's pairs and the joins of array bodies (switch-over-
# distance-flat.md section 5).
set -u

OUT=${1:-}
if [ -z "$OUT" ] ; then echo "usage: $0 <out-file> [scratch-dir] [any|walk|compile]" >&2 ; exit 1 ; fi
case "$OUT" in /*) ;; *) OUT="$PWD/$OUT" ;; esac
FH=${FORTRESS_HOME:-$PWD}
D="$FH/explorations/coordinator/tools/distance"
SCRATCH=${2:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/distance.$$}
case "$SCRATCH" in /*) ;; *) SCRATCH="$PWD/$SCRATCH" ;; esac

content.content:
case "$SCRATCH" in /*) ;; *) SCRATCH="$PWD/$SCRATCH" ;; esac
SETTING=${3:-any}
case "$SETTING" in any|walk|compile) ;; *) echo "distance: unknown setting $SETTING" >&2 ; exit 1 ;; esac
FLAGS="-Dprobe.tolerant=true -Dprobe.all=true -Dfortress.analyzer.overload.cache=false"
COMPONENTS="Library/FortressLibrary.fss Library/RangeInternals.fss ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss
 ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/NativeArray.fss Library/List.fss Library/String.fss Library/FlatString.fss Library/Stream.fss
 ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/NatReflect.fss Library/TypeProxy.fss Library/Writer.fss ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss"

rm -rf "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes" "$SCRATCH/classes" "$SCRATCH/caches" "$SCRATCH/tmp"
mkdir -p "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes" "$SCRATCH/classes" "$SCRATCH/caches" "$SCRATCH/tmp" \
         "$(dirname "$OUT")" || exit 1
CP=$("$FH/bin/fortress_classpath" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | sed 's#:[^:]*/default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache##')
if [ -z "$CP" ] ; then echo "distance: no classpath from bin/fortress_classpath" >&2 ; exit 1 ; fi
MACHINE="nproc=$(nproc); $(grep -m1 'model name' /proc/cpuinfo | sed 's/^[^:]*: *//'); $(grep -m1 'cpu MHz' /proc/cpuinfo | sed 's/^[^:]*: *//') MHz; load at start $(cut -d' ' -f1-3 /proc/loadavg); $(java -version 2>&1 | head -1); FORTRESS_THREADS=${FORTRESS_THREADS:-unset}"

# 1. the shadows, from the tracked sources (perf-probes/prelude/switch-over-distance/make-shadows.sh's
#    steps), and the driver; a text edit that no longer matches is the one way this can go stale
SHADOW="every shadow edit matched the tracked sources"
if ! ( cd "$FH" && python3 "$D/shadow-patch.py" ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" \
                && python3 "$D/add-patch.py" "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" ) > "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" 2>&1 ; then
    SHADOW="STALE: a shadow edit no longer matches the tracked sources: $(grep -E '^AssertionError' "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" | tail -1 | tr -s ' ' | cut -c1-200); see $SCRATCH/shadows.txt"
elif ! javac -nowarn -encoding UTF-8 -cp "$CP" -d "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/TypeCheckPhase.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/DesugarPhase.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/CodeGenerationPhase.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/Desugarer.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/nodes_util/NodeComparator.java" >> "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" 2>&1 ; then
    SHADOW="STALE: the shadow sources no longer compile against the tree; see $SCRATCH/shadows.txt"
elif ! javac -nowarn -cp "$CP" -d "$SCRATCH/classes" "$D/DistanceMulti.java" >> "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" 2>&1 ; then
    SHADOW="STALE: DistanceMulti.java no longer compiles against the tree; see $SCRATCH/shadows.txt"
fi

# 2. the run: one JVM, the twelve components, FortressLibrary first so that its run checks
#    the twelve apis with every stage (DistanceMulti.java's header)
RC=
case "$SHADOW" in
  STALE*) : > "$SCRATCH/run.txt" ;;
  *) S=$(date +%s)
     ( cd "$FH" && timeout -k 30 5400 java -Xmx4g -Xss64m -XX:-OmitStackTraceInFastThrow \
           -Djava.io.tmpdir="$SCRATCH/tmp" -Dfortress.caches="$SCRATCH/caches" $FLAGS \
           -cp "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes:$SCRATCH/classes:$CP" DistanceMulti -order check -setting "$SETTING" $COMPONENTS
     ) > "$SCRATCH/run.txt" 2>&1
     RC=$? ; ELAPSED=$(( $(date +%s) - S ))
     rm -rf "$SCRATCH/caches" "$SCRATCH/tmp" ;;
esac

# 3. the table. errors.py's tally and its one-row-per-error list stay in the scratch
#    directory for whoever needs the sites (compare-sites, the review); table.py's rows go
#    into the table, and their total is checked against errors.py's own count.
{
    printf '#distance\tsetting %s; %s; %s\n' "$SETTING" "$FLAGS" "$(echo $COMPONENTS | wc -w) components in one JVM (DistanceMulti -order check)"
    if grep -q '^### all seconds=' "$SCRATCH/run.txt" ; then
        python3 -B "$D/table.py" "$SCRATCH/run.txt" "$FH" > "$SCRATCH/rows.txt" 2>&1
        cat "$SCRATCH/rows.txt"
        python3 "$D/errors.py" "$SCRATCH/errors.tsv" "$SCRATCH/run.txt" > "$SCRATCH/tally.txt" 2>&1
        E=$(sed -n 's/^# \([0-9]*\) distinct errors.*/\1/p' "$SCRATCH/tally.txt")
        T=$(awk -F'\t' '$1 == "#total" { print $2 }' "$SCRATCH/rows.txt")
        [ "$E" = "$T" ] || printf '#check\terrors.py counts %s, table.py %s: the two normalisations differ on this run; see %s\n' "$E" "$T" "$SCRATCH/tally.txt"
        printf '#seconds\t%s\tFortressLibrary %s\n' "${ELAPSED:-?}" "$(sed -n 's/^### done Library\/FortressLibrary.fss rc=[0-9]* seconds=\([0-9]*\)$/\1/p' "$SCRATCH/run.txt")"
    else
        case "$SHADOW" in
          STALE*) printf '#total\tnone: the checker did not run\n' ;;
          *) printf '#total\tnone: the run ended without its last line (rc=%s); see %s\n' "${RC:-?}" "$SCRATCH/run.txt" ;;
        esac
    fi
    printf '#machine\t%s\n' "$MACHINE"
    printf '#shadow\t%s\n' "$SHADOW"
} > "$OUT"

cat "$OUT"
echo "# distance: full output $SCRATCH/run.txt, rc=${RC:-not run}; errors.py's tally $SCRATCH/tally.txt"
grep -q '^#total	[0-9]' "$OUT"

97	  /* A size with each operation whose operands are numerals computed: 2 3 is
98	   * 6, s0 s1 stays s0 s1.  The run time computes the same operations
99	   * (Naming.sizeOp); an operation it does not compute is kept as written.
100	   */
101	  def foldSize(e: IntExpr): IntExpr = e match {
102	    case b@SIntBinaryOp(info, paren, l, r, op) =>
103	      (foldSize(l), foldSize(r)) match {
104	        case (x: IntBase, y: IntBase) =>
105	          val v = com.sun.fortress.runtimeSystem.Naming.sizeOp(op.getText, x.getIntVal.getIntVal, y.getIntVal.getIntVal)
106	          if (v == null) SIntBinaryOp(info, paren, x, y, op)
107	          else NodeFactory.makeIntBase(NodeUtil.getSpan(b), paren,
108	                 com.sun.fortress.nodes_util.ExprFactory.makeIntLiteralExpr(NodeUtil.getSpan(b), v))
109	        case (x, y) => SIntBinaryOp(info, paren, x, y, op)
110	      }
111	    case _ => e
112	  }

114	  /* Two sizes are equal when their written forms are, once numerals are
115	   * folded: the same inference variable, the same static parameter, the same
116	   * number, or the same operation on equal sizes; s0 s1 is not s1 s0.  The
117	   * generated equals compares source positions, so it is not used.
118	   */
119	  def nEq(a: IntExpr, b: IntExpr): Boolean = sameSize(foldSize(a), foldSize(b))
120	
121	  private def sameSize(a: IntExpr, b: IntExpr): Boolean = (a, b) match {
122	    case (x: _InferenceVarInt, y: _InferenceVarInt) => x.getId eq y.getId
123	    case (x: IntRef, y: IntRef) => x.getName.getText == y.getName.getText
124	    case (x: IntBase, y: IntBase) => x.getIntVal.getIntVal == y.getIntVal.getIntVal
125	    case (SIntBinaryOp(_, _, l1, r1, o1), SIntBinaryOp(_, _, l2, r2, o2)) =>
126	      o1.getText == o2.getText && sameSize(l1, l2) && sameSize(r1, r2)
127	    case _ => false
128	  }
129	
130	  /* Two sizes known to differ: two different numerals, or two different
131	   * static parameters.  A name or an operation beside a numeral or an
132	   * operation may be equal to it, as the specification's Q&A on overloaded
133	   * operators answers (n+1 beside 0); nEq says when it is.
134	   */
135	  def nDiffer(a: IntExpr, b: IntExpr): Boolean = (foldSize(a), foldSize(b)) match {
136	    case (x: IntBase, y: IntBase) => !sameSize(x, y)
137	    case (x: IntRef, y: IntRef) => !sameSize(x, y) && !isOpenedSize(x) && !isOpenedSize(y)
138	    case _ => false
139	  }

142	   * at every n, and a value of the trait passed where N[\m\] is expected binds
143	   * m to its own size, a name no program can write, equal only to itself and
144	   * not known to differ from any size (TypeAnalyzer.openWhereSizes).
145	   */
146	  private val openedSizeMark = "#"
147	  private val openedSizes = new java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger()
148	  def openedSizeName(where: String): String = where + openedSizeMark + openedSizes.incrementAndGet

150	    case r: IntRef => r.getName.getText.contains(openedSizeMark)

162	    val TPrimitive(pl1, nl1, pu1, nu1, pe1, ne1) = p

184	  def and(c1: CFormula, c2: CFormula)(implicit ta: TypeAnalyzer): CFormula = (c1, c2) match {
185	    case (True, _) => reduce(c2)
186	    case (False, _) => False
187	    case (And(as, os, ms), And(bs, ps, qs)) =>
188	      reduce(And(merge(as, bs, tMerge, tUnit), merge(os, ps, oMerge, oUnit), merge(ms, qs, nMerge, nUnit)))
189	    case (Or(cs), Or(ds)) =>
190	      dis(for(c <- cs; d <- ds) yield and(c,d))
191	    case (c1: Or, c2: And) => and(c1, Or(Set(c2)))
192	    case _ => and(c2, c1)
193	  }

195	  def and(e1: EFormula, e2: EFormula)(implicit ta: TypeAnalyzer): EFormula = (e1, e2) match {
196	    case (True, _) => reduce(e2)
197	    case (False, _) => False
198	    case (Conjuncts(as, os, ms), Conjuncts(bs, ps, qs)) => reduce(Conjuncts(as ++ bs, os ++ ps, ms ++ qs))
199	    case (Disjuncts(e1), Disjuncts(e2)) => 
200	      dis(for(c <- e1; d <- e2) yield and(c,d))
201	    case (e1: Disjuncts, e2: Conjuncts) => and(e1, Disjuncts(Set(e2)))
202	    case _ => and(e2, e1)
203	  }

211	  def or(c1: CFormula, c2: CFormula)(implicit ta: TypeAnalyzer): CFormula = (c1, c2) match {
212	    case (True, _) => True
213	    case (False, _) => reduce(c2)
214	    case (Or(cs), Or(ds)) => reduce(Or(cs ++ ds))
215	    case (a: And, b: And) => reduce(Or(Set(a, b)))
216	    case (a: And, Or(cs)) => reduce(Or(cs ++ Set(a)))
217	    case _ => or(c2, c1)
218	  }

220	  def or(e1: EFormula, e2: EFormula)(implicit ta: TypeAnalyzer): EFormula = (e1, e2) match {
221	    case (True, _) => True

223	    case (Disjuncts(e1s), Disjuncts(e2s)) => reduce(Disjuncts(e1s ++ e2s))
224	    case (a: Conjuncts, b: Conjuncts) => reduce(Disjuncts(Set(a, b)))
225	    case (a: Conjuncts, Disjuncts(es)) => reduce(Disjuncts(es ++ Set(a)))
226	    case _ => or(e2, e1)

239	  private def imp(c1: CFormula, c2: CFormula, debug:Boolean=false)(implicit ta: TypeAnalyzer): Boolean = {
240	    if (debug)
241	      println("imp: c1 = " + c1 + ", c2 = " + c2)
242	    val result = (c1, c2) match {
243	  
244	    case (False, _) => true
245	    case (_, False) => false
246	    case (_, True) => true
247	    case (True, _) => false
248	    // Checks whether every constraint in c2 is in c1
249	    case (And(as, os, ms), And(bs, ps, qs)) => {
250	       val a1 = forall(as, bs, tImplies, tUnit)
251	       val a2 = forall(ps, os, oImplies, oUnit)
252	       val a3 = forall(ms, qs, nImplies, nUnit)
253	       if (debug)
254	         println("a1, a2, a3 = " + a1 + ", " + a2 + ", " + a3)
255	       a1 && a2 && a3
256	    }
257	    case (c1, Or(cs)) => cs.exists(imp(c1, _))
258	    case (Or(cs), c2) => cs.forall(imp(_, c2))
259	    }
260	    if (debug)
261	      println("imp: result = " + result)
262	    result
263	  }

265	  private def tImplies(p: TPrimitive, q: TPrimitive)(implicit ta: TypeAnalyzer): Boolean = {
266	    val TPrimitive(pl1, nl1, pu1, nu1, pe1, ne1) = p
267	    val TPrimitive(pl2, nl2, pu2, nu2, pe2, ne2) = q
268	    val pls = ta.lteq(ta.join(pl2), ta.join(pl1))
269	    val nls = nl2.forall(n2 => nl1.exists(ta.lteq(n2,_)) || pe1.exists(p1 => ta.definitelyExcludes(p1, n2)) || pu1.exists(p1 => isFalse(ta.subtype(n2, p1))))
270	    val pus = ta.lteq(ta.meet(pu1), ta.meet(pu2))
271	    val nus = nu2.forall(n2 => nu1.exists(ta.lteq(_,n2)) || pe1.exists(p1 => ta.definitelyExcludes(p1, n2)) || pl1.exists(p1 => isFalse(ta.subtype(p1, n2))))
272	//         // ToDo: Figure out whether using a recursive implies here will terminate
273	//         val pes = pe2.forall(e2 => pe1.exists(ta.lteq(e2, _)) || pu1.exists(t1 => imp(c1, ta.excludes(e2, t1))))
274	    // Actually, it won't.  So we need to make sure that c1 is also decomposed.  So we use a specialized imp called primImp.
275	    val pes = pe2.forall(e2 => pe1.exists(ta.lteq(e2, _)) || pu1.exists(t1 => primImp(p, ta.excludes(e2, t1))))
276	    val nes = ne2.forall(n2 => pu1.exists(ta.lteq(_, n2)) || pl1.exists(p1 => isFalse(ta.excludes(p1, n2))))
277	    pls && nls && pus && nus && pes && nes
278	 }

280	  private def primImp(p: TPrimitive, c2: CFormula)(implicit ta: TypeAnalyzer): Boolean = c2 match {
281	    case (False) => false
282	    case (True) => true
283	    case (And(bs, ps, qs)) => bs.values.forall(tImplies(p, _))
284	    case (Or(cs)) => cs.exists(primImp(p, _))
285	  }

289	   val OPrimitive(p2s, n2s) = q

301	  private def forall[S, T](as: Map[S, T], bs: Map[S,T], pred: (T, T) => Boolean, unit: T): Boolean = {
302	    stackLevel += 1
303	    if (stackLevel == 10) bug("forall stack overflow")
304	    val result = (as.keySet ++ bs.keySet).forall(k => pred(as.getOrElse(k, unit), bs.getOrElse(k, unit)))
305	    stackLevel -= 1
306	    result
307	  }

312	  private def imp(e1: EFormula, e2: EFormula)(implicit ta: TypeAnalyzer): Boolean = (e1, e2) match {
313	    case (False, _) => true
314	    case (_, False) => false
315	    case (_, True) => true
316	    case (True, _) => false
317	    case (Conjuncts(as, os, ms), Conjuncts(bs, ps, qs)) =>
318	      implies(as, bs, ta.equiv) && implies(os, ps, oEq) && implies(ms, qs, nEq)
319	    case (_, Disjuncts(es)) => es.exists(imp(e1, _))
320	    case (Disjuncts(es), _) => es.forall(imp(_, e2))
321	  }

343	  private def removeDups[T](s: Set[T], eq: (T, T)=> Boolean) = 
344	    s.foldLeft(Set[T]()){(ns, i) =>
345	      if(ns.exists(eq(i, _)))
346	        ns
347	      else
348	        ns ++ Set(i)
349	    }

356	  def reduce(c: CFormula)(implicit ta: TypeAnalyzer): CFormula =  c match {
357	    case And(ts, os, ns) =>
358	      def tSimplify(ip: (_InferenceVarType, TPrimitive)): Option[(_InferenceVarType, TPrimitive)] = ip match {
359	        // catch trivial contradictions 
360	        case (i, TPrimitive(pl,nl,pu,nu,pe,ne)) 
361	          if (nl.contains(i) || nu.contains(i) || pe.contains(i) || 
362	              nl.contains(BOTTOM)|| ne.contains(BOTTOM) || nu.contains(ANY)) =>
363	            None
364	        case (i, TPrimitive(pl,nl,pu,nu,pe,ne))
365	          if (pe.contains(ANY)) =>
366	            tSimplify(i, TPrimitive(pl, nl, Set(BOTTOM), nu, Set(), ne))
367	        case (i, TPrimitive(pl,nl,pu,nu,pe,ne)) =>
368	          Some((i, TPrimitive(maxTypes(pl.filter(_!=i)), minTypes(nl) ++ nl.filter(_==ANY), 
369	                                      minTypes(pu.filter(_!=i)) , maxTypes(nu) ++ nu.filter(_==BOTTOM), 
370	                                      maxTypes(pe), minTypes(ne) ++ ne.filter(_==ANY))))
371	      }
372	      // Comprises means there are more of these
373	      def tContradiction(ip: (_InferenceVarType, TPrimitive)) = {
374	        val TPrimitive(pl,nl,pu,nu,pe,ne) = ip._2
375	        if(isFalse(ta.subtype(ta.join(pl), ta.meet(pu))) ||
376	           nl.exists(n => pl.exists(ta.lteq(n, _))) ||
377	           nu.exists(n => pu.exists(ta.lteq(_, n))) ||
378	           pe.exists(e => pu.exists(ta.lteq(_,e))) ||
379	           pl.exists(l => pe.exists(e => isFalse(ta.excludes(l,e)))) ||
380	           ne.exists(n => pe.exists(ta.lteq(n, _))) ||
381	           ne.exists(n => pu.exists(ta.definitelyExcludes(n, _))))
382	          None
383	        else
384	          Some(ip)
385	      }
386	      def tRedundant(ip: (_InferenceVarType, TPrimitive)) = {
387	        val TPrimitive(pl,nl,pu,nu,pe,ne) = ip._2
388	        Some((ip._1, TPrimitive(pl,
389	                       nl.filterNot(n => pu.exists(p => isFalse(ta.subtype(n, p)))).
390	                          filterNot(n => pe.exists(ta.definitelyExcludes(n, _))),
391	                       pu,
392	                       nu.filterNot(n => pl.exists(p => isFalse(ta.subtype(p, n)))).
393	                          filterNot(n => pe.exists(ta.definitelyExcludes(n, _))),
394	                       pe.filterNot(p => pu.exists(ta.definitelyExcludes(p, _))),
395	                       ne.filterNot(n => pu.exists(ta.lteq(_, n))).
396	                          filterNot(n => pl.exists(p => isFalse(ta.excludes(p, n)))))))
397	      }
398	      def tTrivial(ip: (_InferenceVarType, TPrimitive)) = {
399	        val TPrimitive(pl,nl,pu,nu,pe,ne) = ip._2
400	        pl.isEmpty && nl.isEmpty && pu.isEmpty && nu.isEmpty && pe.isEmpty && ne.isEmpty
401	      }
402	      def oSimplify(ip: (_InferenceVarOp, OPrimitive)) = {
403	        val (i, OPrimitive(ps, ns)) = ip
404	        val sps = removeDups(ps - i, oEq)
405	        val sns = removeDups(ns, oEq)
406	        (i, OPrimitive(sps, sns))
407	      }
408	      def oContradiction(ip: (_InferenceVarOp, OPrimitive)) = {
409	        val (i, OPrimitive(ps, ns)) = ip
410	        if(ns.contains(i) || ps.exists(p => ns.contains(p)) || ps.filterNot(_.isInstanceOf[_InferenceVarOp]).size > 1)
411	          None
412	        else
413	          Some(ip)
414	      }
415	      def oTrivial(ip: (_InferenceVarOp, OPrimitive)) = {
416	        val (i, OPrimitive(ps, ns)) = ip
417	        ps.isEmpty && ns.isEmpty
418	      }
419	      def nSimplify(ip: (_InferenceVarInt, NPrimitive)) = {
420	        val (i, NPrimitive(ps, ns)) = ip
421	        (i, NPrimitive(removeDups(ps.filterNot(nEq(i, _)), nEq), removeDups(ns, nEq)))
422	      }
423	      // A size variable equal to two different sizes, or to arithmetic, has no solution
424	      def nContradiction(ip: (_InferenceVarInt, NPrimitive)) = {
425	        val (i, NPrimitive(ps, ns)) = ip
426	        if(ns.exists(nEq(i, _)) || ps.exists(p => ns.exists(nEq(p, _))) ||
427	           ps.exists(p => !isNatTerm(p) && !p.isInstanceOf[_InferenceVarInt]) ||
428	           removeDups(ps.filterNot(_.isInstanceOf[_InferenceVarInt]), nEq).size > 1)
429	          None
430	        else
431	          Some(ip)
432	      }
433	      def nTrivial(ip: (_InferenceVarInt, NPrimitive)) = {
434	        val (i, NPrimitive(ps, ns)) = ip
435	        ps.isEmpty && ns.isEmpty
436	      }
437	      val nts = ts.map(tSimplify).map(_.flatMap(tContradiction)).map(_.flatMap(tRedundant)).map(_.getOrElse(return False)).filterNot(tTrivial)
438	      val nos = os.map(oSimplify).map(oContradiction).map(_.getOrElse(return False)).filterNot(oTrivial)
439	      val nns = ns.map(nSimplify).map(nContradiction).map(_.getOrElse(return False)).filterNot(nTrivial)
440	      if (nts.isEmpty && nos.isEmpty && nns.isEmpty)
441	        return True
442	      else
443	        And(Map(nts.toSeq: _*), Map(nos.toSeq: _*), Map(nns.toSeq: _*)) 
444	    case Or(cs) =>
445	      val rcs = cs.map(reduce(_))
446	      if(rcs.contains(True))
447	        True
448	      else {
449	        val ncs = maximalCFormulas(rcs)
450	        ncs.size match {
451	          case 0 => False
452	          case 1 => ncs.head
453	          case _ => Or(ncs.asInstanceOf[Set[And]])
454	        }
455	      }
456	    case _ => c
457	  }

459	  private def minTypes(s: Set[Type])(implicit ta: TypeAnalyzer) =
460	      TU.conjuncts(ta.meet(s))

465	  def reduce(e: EFormula)(implicit ta: TypeAnalyzer): EFormula = e match {
466	    case Conjuncts(as, os, ms) => 
467	      val ras = reduce(as, ta.equiv).map{x => removeDups(x, (a: Type, b: Type) => ta.equiv(a, b))}.
468	        filter{_.size > 1}
469	      val ros = reduce(os, (a: Op, b: Op) => a==b).map{
470	        x => removeDups(x, (a: Op, b: Op) => a==b)}.
471	        filter{_.size > 1}
472	      val rns = reduce(ms, nEq).map{x => removeDups(x, nEq)}.filter{_.size > 1}
473	      if(ras.isEmpty && ros.isEmpty && rns.isEmpty)
474	        True
475	      else if(isContradictory(ras, (s: Type, t: Type) => isFalse(ta.equivalent(s,t)))
476	              || isContradictory(ros, definitelyNotEqual)
477	              || isContradictory(rns, definitelyNotEqualNat))
478	        False
479	      else
480	        Conjuncts(ras, ros, rns)  
481	    case True => True
482	    case False => False
483	    case Disjuncts(es) => 
484	      val nes = es.map(reduce).filter{_.isInstanceOf[Conjuncts]}
485	      nes.size match {
486	        case 0 => False
487	        case 1 => nes.head
488	        case _ => Disjuncts(nes.asInstanceOf[Set[Conjuncts]])
489	      }
490	  }

492	  private def definitelyNotEqual(a: Op, b: Op): Boolean = (a, b) match {
493	    case (_: _InferenceVarOp, _) => false
494	    case (_, _:_InferenceVarOp) => false
495	    case _ => a!=b
496	  }
497	
498	  private def definitelyNotEqualNat(a: IntExpr, b: IntExpr): Boolean = (a, b) match {
499	    case (_: _InferenceVarInt, _) => false
500	    case (_, _:_InferenceVarInt) => false
501	    case _ => nDiffer(a, b)
502	  }

504	  private def isContradictory[T](as: Set[Set[T]], neq: (T,T) => Boolean): Boolean =
505	    !as.isEmpty && as.forall{a =>  !a.isEmpty && a.tail.foldLeft((a.head, false)){case ((s, b), t) => (t, neq(s,t) || b)}._2}
506	  /*
507	   * Given a set of sets of Ts that are supposed to represent
508	   * equivalence classes, this method merges together any classes
509	   * that share a T to give a reduced set of sets of Ts.
510	   */
511	  
512	  private def reduce[T](es: Set[Set[T]], eq: (T,T)=>Boolean): Set[Set[T]] = {
513	    def binReduce(e1: Set[T], es: Set[Set[T]]): Set[Set[T]] = 
514	      if(es.isEmpty)
515	        Set(e1)
516	      else {
517	        // Since es is reduced there will be 0 or 1 matches
518	        val e2 = es.filter(e => e.exists(a => e1.exists(eq(_, a)))).headOption
519	        val nes = es.filterNot(e => e.exists(a => e1.exists(eq(_, a))))
520	        Set(e2.getOrElse(Set()) ++ e1) ++ nes
521	      }
522	    es.foldLeft(Set[Set[T]]()){(a, b) => binReduce(b, a)}
523	  }

525	  /*
526	   * Solves a constraint formula by first unifying away all the equality constraints
527	   * and then using Dan's simple algorithm from "Java Type Inference is Broken." Dan's
528	   * algorithm does not do very well when inference variables have bounds that contain
529	   * other inference variables such as those that arise from the self type idiom. At some
530	   * point it would be a good idea to replace this with a smarter algorithm.
531	   */
532	  
533	  def solve(c: CFormula)(implicit ta: TypeAnalyzer): Option[(Type => Type, Op => Op, IntExpr => IntExpr)] = 
534	    slv(reduce(c), false)
535	
536	  /*
537	   * Solves a constraint formula on the static arguments of a call. A type
538	   * inference variable that no lower bound fixes takes the intersection of its
539	   * upper bounds, its declared bound and what the expected type requires, and
540	   * one the formula leaves unconstrained takes Any; none takes BottomType, and a
541	   * lower bound BottomType fixes nothing.
542	   */
543	  def solveToBounds(c: CFormula)(implicit ta: TypeAnalyzer): Option[(Type => Type, Op => Op, IntExpr => IntExpr)] =
544	    slv(reduce(c), true)
545	  
546	  private def slv(c: CFormula, toBounds: Boolean)(implicit ta: TypeAnalyzer): Option[(Type => Type, Op => Op, IntExpr => IntExpr)] = c match {
547	    // False cannot be solved
548	    case False => None
549	    // True has the trivial solution
550	    case True => Some((if (toBounds) TU.topIvars else tEmptySub, oEmptySub, nEmptySub))
551	    // We solve an Or by solving one of its branches
552	    case Or(cs) => 
553	      for (e <- cs) {
554	        val se = slv(e, toBounds)
555	        if(se.isDefined)
556	          return se
557	      }
558	      None
559	    /* To solve an And:
560	     * 1) Factor the constraint formula into the conjunction of an equality constraint E
561	     * and additional constraints I
562	     * 2) Find the principal unifier U of E
563	     * 3) Apply U to I to get I'
564	     * TODO: We can solve more constraints if we iterate 1), 2) 3) until we hit a fixed point but we must be careful to ensure termination
565	     * 4) Solve I' to get a substitution S
566	     * 5) Return S composed with U
567	     */
568	    case _:And => 
569	      val (newCon, tUnifier, oUnifier, nUnifier) = unify(c).getOrElse(return None)
570	      newCon match {
571	        case True => Some((if (toBounds) TU.topIvars compose tUnifier else tUnifier, oUnifier, nUnifier))
572	        case False => None
573	        case nc0@And(ts, os, ns) =>
574	//	  println("nc: " + nc0)
575	          // Operators only have equality constraints so they should always be solved by unification
576	          assert(os.isEmpty)
577	          // So do sizes: an equality left over has no solution, and a size
578	          // with only disequalities left is left unsolved
579	          if (ns.exists{case (_, NPrimitive(pe, _)) => !pe.isEmpty}) return None
580	          val nc = And(ts, os)
581	          def boundOnly(p: TPrimitive) =
582	            toBounds && p.pl.forall(l => TU.hasInferenceVars(l) || l.isInstanceOf[BottomType])
583	          val lowered = ts.filterNot(e => boundOnly(e._2)).map{
584	              case (k, p@TPrimitive(pl,nl,pu,nu,pe,ne)) => {
585	                var uni = ta.join(pl.filterNot(TU.hasInferenceVars))
586	                // Heuristic extension to Dan Smith's algorithm:
587	                // If there is a single lower bound and it is a trait type, 
588	                // try all of its ancestors, searching for one that satisfies
589	                // all upper bounds.
590	//		println("uni: " + uni)
591	//		println("pl: " + pl)
592	                if (pl.size == 1) {
593	                  pl.head match {
594	                    case tt:TraitType =>
595	                      for (a <- (ta.ancestors(tt) ++ List(uni)).toList.sortWith((a,b) => isTrue(ta.subtype(b,a)))) {
596			        val proposedMap = cMap(nc, TU.killIvars compose tSubstitution(Map((k,p)).map(_=>(k,a))))
597	//			println("For ancestor " + a + " proposed map is " + proposedMap)
598	                        if (isTrue(proposedMap)) {
599	                          uni = a 
600	                        }
601	                      }
602	                    case _ => 0
603	                  }
604	                }
605	//                println("slv: new (k->uni) = " + k + "->" + uni)
606	                (k, uni)
607	              }
608	            }.toMap
609	          // A variable that no lower bound fixes takes the meet of its upper bounds, each
610	          // at the solutions of the other variables it mentions once those are found, as a
611	          // bound that mentions another static parameter is taken at that parameter's
612	          // instance; a bound that still mentions a variable, the variable itself among
613	          // them, is left out.
614	          var solved: Map[_InferenceVarType, Type] = lowered
615	          var pending = ts.toList.filter(e => boundOnly(e._2))
616	          def waits(k: _InferenceVarType, p: TPrimitive) =
617	            p.pu.exists(u => TU.getInferenceVars(tSubstitution(solved)(u)).exists(v => v != k && pending.exists(_._1 == v)))
618	          var ready = pending.filterNot(e => waits(e._1, e._2))
619	          while (ready.nonEmpty || pending.nonEmpty) {
620	            val now = if (ready.nonEmpty) ready else pending
621	            val known = tSubstitution(solved)
622	            for ((k, p) <- now) {
623	              val upper = ta.meet(p.pu.map(known).filterNot(TU.hasInferenceVars))
624	              if (upper.isInstanceOf[BottomType]) return None
625	              solved = solved + (k -> upper)
626	            }
627	            pending = pending.filterNot(e => now.exists(_._1 == e._1))
628	            ready = pending.filterNot(e => waits(e._1, e._2))
629	          }
630	          val sub = (if (toBounds) TU.topIvars else TU.killIvars) compose tSubstitution(solved)
631		  val newMap = cMap(nc, sub)
632	//	  println("newMap: " + newMap)
633	          if(isTrue(newMap))
634	            Some((sub compose tUnifier, oUnifier, nUnifier))
635	          else {
636	//               println("sub:" + sub + " on formula " + c)
637	               None
638	          }
639	        // Should never occur
640	        case _:Or => bug("Applied a substitution to an And and got an Or")
641	      }      
642	  }

644	  def unify(c: CFormula)(implicit ta: TypeAnalyzer): Option[(CFormula, Type => Type, Op => Op, IntExpr => IntExpr)] = {
645	      val eq = getEquality(c)
646	//      println("Unify " + c + " produces " + eq)
647	      un(eq).map{case (ts, os, ns) => (cMap(c, ts, os, ns), ts, os, ns)}
648	  }

650	  def unifyWithDebug(c: CFormula, debug:Boolean=false)(implicit ta: TypeAnalyzer): Option[(CFormula, Type => Type, Op => Op, IntExpr => IntExpr)] = {
651	      val eq = getEquality(c)
652	      if (debug)
653	          println("Unify " + c + " produces " + eq)
654	      un(eq).map{case (ts, os, ns) => (cMapWithDebug(c, ts, os, ns, debug), ts, os, ns)}
655	  }

657	  /*
658	   * This method factors all of the type equalities out of an inequality constraint
659	   * since they are better solved through unification than the algorithm in Dan Smith's
660	   * "Java Type Inference is Broken" paper.
661	   */
662	  
663	  private def getEquality(c: CFormula)(implicit ta: TypeAnalyzer): EFormula = reduce(c) match {
664	    case False => False
665	    case True => True
666	    case And(ts, os, ns) =>
667	      val teq = getCliques[Type, TPrimitive, _InferenceVarType](ts, 
668	          {case TPrimitive(pl,nl,pu,nu,pe,ne) => pl.filter(a => pu.exists(b => ta.equiv(a, b))) ++ pu.filter(a => pl.exists(b => ta.equiv(a, b)))})
669	      val oeq = getCliques[Op, OPrimitive, _InferenceVarOp](os,
670	          {case OPrimitive(ps, ns) => ps})
671	      val neq = getCliques[IntExpr, NPrimitive, _InferenceVarInt](ns,
672	          {case NPrimitive(ps, _) => ps})
673	      reduce(Conjuncts(teq, oeq, neq))
674	    case Or(cs) => 
675	      val eq = cs.map(getEquality)
676	      dis(eq)
677	  }
678	  
679	  private def getCliques[S,T, U <: S](xs: Map[U, T], makeClique: T => Set[S]): Set[Set[S]] = {
680	    xs.map{case (a, b) => makeClique(b) ++ Set(a)}.toSet
681	  }
682	  
683	  private def dis(eq: Set[EFormula])(implicit ta: TypeAnalyzer): EFormula = {
684	    if (eq.exists(isTrue(_)))
685	      True
686	    else
687	      reduce(Disjuncts(eq.filter(_.isInstanceOf[Conjuncts]).asInstanceOf[Set[Conjuncts]]))
688	  }
689	  
690	  private def dis(cs: Set[CFormula])(implicit ta: TypeAnalyzer): CFormula = {
691	    if(cs.exists(isTrue(_)))
692	      True
693	    else
694	      reduce(Or(cs.filter(_.isInstanceOf[And]).asInstanceOf[Set[And]]))
695	  }
